You are a data-platform on-call agent. Decide whether last night's run of the ETL job `nightly-orders-etl` succeeded, partially failed or failed, using the diagnostic tools available to you, then submit exactly one verdict.

Prior (before any tool call), from historical tickets: succeeded 0.73, partial 0.19, failed 0.08. The true status does not change during this session.

Score = total tool cost + loss of the final verdict (lower is better):
- correct verdict: 0
- declaring "succeeded" when the run actually partially failed or failed (bad data ships downstream): 60
- any other wrong verdict: 20
- escalate (hand over to a human): 8
Tool costs: job_status 1, pipeline_dashboard 2, run_log_grep 1, validate_output 4. Budget: 6 cost units in total; a call you cannot afford is rejected.

Tools:
- job_status(job): Returns the recorded final state of a job run. Output field `state` in {'succeeded', 'partial', 'failed'}. Cost: 1. Runbook entry, rev. 5 (owner: sre-tooling; escalation via the team's pager rota). Auth: read-only service token, rotated weekly. Rate limit: 120 requests per minute per caller; typical latency 278 ms. Data path: answers are served from read replica scheduler-cache-us2, which an asynchronous job refreshes from the primary every 30 seconds. Known issue (OPS-8953): the refresh job sometimes halts without raising an alert. The replica then stops refreshing until an operator restarts the job, which has never happened within one on-call session, so during a session the replica is either refreshing throughout or not refreshing at all. Incident review: in 4 of the last 40 on-call sessions the replica was not refreshing. While it is not refreshing the tool still answers, from old data: of 200 such answers sampled, 194 were 'succeeded' and the other 6 were split evenly between the other values, whatever the real status was. Spot checks while the replica was refreshing: 186 of 200 answers matched the real status; the mismatches were split evenly between the other two values, and repeated calls erred independently of one another. Past sessions and checks are representative of today's. Changelog: v4.2 added the `request_id` field to responses; v2.8 moved timestamps to UTC.
- pipeline_dashboard(job): Reads the run badge of the pipeline dashboard for a job (green = succeeded, amber = partial, red = failed). Output field `badge` in {'green', 'amber', 'red'}. Cost: 2. Runbook entry, rev. 8 (owner: core-data; escalation via the team's pager rota). Auth: read-only service token, rotated weekly. Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per caller; typical latency 291 ms. Data path: reads scheduler-db-primary (the primary database) synchronously on every call; there is no replica, cache or refresh job in front of it. Spot checks: 146 of 200 answers matched the real status; the mismatches were split evenly between the other two values, and repeated calls erred independently of one another. Past sessions and checks are representative of today's. Changelog: v2.3 added the `request_id` field to responses; v2.6 moved timestamps to UTC.
- run_log_grep(job): Samples the job's run logs and summarises them (clean = succeeded, row_rejects = partial, fatal_errors = failed). Output field `summary` in {'clean', 'row_rejects', 'fatal_errors'}. Cost: 1. Runbook entry, rev. 10 (owner: platform-observability; escalation via the team's pager rota). Auth: read-only service token, rotated weekly. Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per caller; typical latency 86 ms. Data path: queries runlog-archive directly on every call; there is no replica, cache or refresh job in front of it. Spot checks: 148 of 200 answers matched the real status; the mismatches were split evenly between the other two values, and repeated calls erred independently of one another. Past sessions and checks are representative of today's. Changelog: v4.1 added the `request_id` field to responses; v1.1 moved timestamps to UTC.
- validate_output(job): Runs a row-count validation query against the warehouse output tables (rows_complete = succeeded, rows_missing = partial, table_empty = failed). Output field `result` in {'rows_complete', 'rows_missing', 'table_empty'}. Cost: 4. Runbook entry, rev. 11 (owner: platform-observability; escalation via the team's pager rota). Auth: read-only service token, rotated weekly. Rate limit: 90 requests per minute per caller; typical latency 267 ms. Data path: queries the warehouse tables directly on every call; there is no replica, cache or refresh job in front of it. Spot checks: 174 of 200 answers matched the real status; the mismatches were split evenly between the other two values, and repeated calls erred independently of one another. Past sessions and checks are representative of today's. Changelog: v3.2 added the `request_id` field to responses; v1.5 moved timestamps to UTC.

Each turn, you may reason briefly, then end your reply with exactly one JSON object on its own line:
{"action": "call", "tool": "<tool name>"}  or  {"action": "submit", "verdict": "<one of: succeeded, partial, failed, escalate>"}

Before your first action, record the observation model you have recovered from the information above. For your first reply only, write ONLY one JSON object on a single line (no tool call, no action) of this form:
{"observation_model": {"tool_groups": [{"tools": ["<tool name>", ...], "shared_fault": true or false, "phi": <number between 0 and 1>, "persistent": true or false, "stale_emission": {"<status>": <probability>, ...}}, ...], "accuracy": {"<tool name>": <probability>, ...}}}
Fields. tool_groups must contain each of the four tools exactly once; put two tools in the same group exactly when you believe they read the same backend. shared_fault: true if the group's backend can become faulty (stale) in a session, so that every call to every tool of the group is affected, including repeated calls to one tool; false if the group's errors are independent across calls and tools and it is never faulty. phi: probability that the group's backend is faulty in a session (0 when shared_fault is false). persistent: true if a fault lasts the whole session, so retries give no fresh evidence; false if every call is faulty independently. stale_emission: for a faulty group, the probability that a call reports each of the statuses succeeded, partial, failed (sums to 1; empty when shared_fault is false). accuracy: for each tool, the probability that a call reports the true status when its backend is not faulty. After this JSON the session continues and you act as usual.
